title: South Park pokes fun at Donald Trump as he's once again shown with tiny manhood - NewsBreak
text: The latest South Park episode has aired, after the political satire cartoon came under fire for its savage depiction of President Donald Trump and the White House. During their season premiere, South Park left no lines uncrossed as they portrayed Trump with a micro-penis, pictured him with his "boyfriend" Satan, and openly mocked his Paramount settlement deal. Now in the latest episode they haven't held back again as they showed Trump at Mar-a-Lago, along with JD Vance and Satan. The episode centered around Mr. Mackey being fired from the school, so he joins Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Supported by the Head of Homeland Security, Kristi Noem, Mr. Mackey is flown to Trump's Florida resort to meet Trump and Vance. READ MORE: Amy Bradley's brother reveals major update in the case after Netflix documentary READ MORE: New Amy Bradley leads emerge following Netflix documentary 27 years later After being greeted by Trump and a tinier Vance, both donning white suits, Mr. Mackey is shown around Mar-A-Lago and follows Trump into a bedroom where Satan is sat in bed, reading. During this, Trump somehow loses his pants, displaying the character's tiny penis. This isn't the first time that the show decided to portray the president's manhood as small. During the premiere two weeks prior to this episode, Trump is posing for a nude painting and when he sees the final result, he angrily asks, "Why is my d--k so small?!" and the artist answers, "That's the size it is in the photo." When Trump is in bed with Satan later in the episode, Satan said, "I can't even see anything it's so small," in reference to the character's appendage. During South Park's season 27 premiere aired on Wednesday, July 23, the series was met with a staggering viewership of 5.9 million fans watching across Paramount+ and Comedy Central. According to new data collected by Nielsen, this season premiere's viewership skyrocketed compared to last season, with +68% more people tuning in. The Trump episode might have been a high for the show, but it's prompted a fierce reaction including from the White House. In response to these episodes, White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers issued a furious statement to Rolling Stone that read, "The Left’s hypocrisy truly has no end — for years they have come after South Park for what they labeled as ‘offense’ [sic] content, but suddenly they are praising the show." Rogers concluded, "President Trump has delivered on more promises in just six months than any other president in our country’s history — and no fourth-rate show can derail President Trump’s hot streak." New South Park episodes air every Wednesday at 10 p.m. ET on Comedy Central and is available for streaming the following day on Paramount+.
